yield_rationale: Phase 3 expansion surfaced 13 novel candidates beyond the 6 Phase 1 Sampler-A holy rows (radiant, blessed, sacred, divine, dawn, sanctum). The non-religious-coded lane was productive: radiance (noun form; R=3), solar, corona, empyrion, gilded, aureate, luminary, corona, halcyon, lambent, stellar, lumen, lucent, and consecrated (religious-coded but novel). The Grim Dawn Order constellation lane yielded Empyrion and Solael as proper-noun non-Christian deity names. Non-religious-coded count: 11 (radiance, solar, corona, aureate, luminary, gilded, lambent, halcyon, stellar, lumen, lucent + empyrion/solael as fictional deity names). Religious-coded count: 4 (blessed, sacred, divine, consecrated). Strong yield toward the non-religious target per gandalf amendment.

source_coverage_breadth.notes: Grim Dawn Oathkeeper is the richest ARPG source for non-religious holy vocabulary: Empyrion (sun deity), Solar Bastion, Empyrion's Light, Solael. The Order devotion lane yielded the most novel non-religious-coded candidates.
PoE Guardian's Radiant Crusade / Radiant Faith passives yield corona, radiance, lucent, lumen, luminary vocabulary. Consecrated Ground is a major novel mechanical-keyword find.
Lost Ark Paladin yields solar, luminary, radiance vocabulary in translated skill descriptions. Moderate additional citations alongside Phase 1 Sampler-A finds.
Diablo series yields gilded gear vocabulary and consecrated-ground skill names. Primary use is confirming Phase 1 candidates (blessed, sacred, divine) with religious-coded framing.
Last Epoch holy passives use halcyon, lucent vocabulary sparsely in passive description text. Thin yield but substrate-coherent.

substrate_tagging_observations: The key contamination pattern in ARPG holy is not cross-primary but cross-register: religious-coded vs non-religious-coded within the same element. All 4 religious-coded candidates (blessed, sacred, divine, consecrated) have R=3 ubiquity; all non-religious-coded astronomical vocabulary (aureate, luminary, halcyon, lambent, stellar, lumen, lucent) has R=1-2 niche recognizability. This creates a tension for Phase 5a synthesis: the high-recognizability substrate is religious-coded; the tone-safe substrate is lower-recognizability. Empyrion and Solael (fictional deity proper-nouns) offer a middle path — moderate recognizability within ARPG fanbase + non-Judeo-Christian framing.
expansion_sub_agent_summary: ARPG × holy Phase 3 expansion successfully filled the non-religious light sub-vocabulary gap gandalf identified. 17 total rows (13 novel). Non-religious-coded candidates: radiance (1), solar (2), corona (3), empyrion (4), gilded (6), aureate (8), stellar (9), lucent (10), lumen (11), halcyon (13), lambent (12), luminary (7) — 12 non-religious-coded total. Religious-coded candidates with flag: consecrated, blessed, sacred, divine — 4 total, all surfaced for completeness per substrate-led discipline. Distribution: non-religious-coded = 12 of 17 (71%); religious-coded = 4 of 17 (23%); ambiguous = 1 (solael as fictional deity). The Grim Dawn Empyrion/Solael lane is the most valuable novel finding: Grim Dawn's Order faction provides fictional-deity proper-nouns for the holy element that are neither Judeo-Christian-coded nor common English words, potentially useful for Phase 5a as isekai-compatible holy vocabulary. Consecrated Ground (PoE mechanic; R=3) is the most recognizable novel religious-coded candidate and should be flagged clearly for PG-3 curation.
